2. The central algorithm: repairing a noisy, initially arbitrary syndrome

The preparation problem differs from ordinary recovery. When preparing a code state by measuring checks on a product state, the true syndrome can be an arbitrary valid syndrome. It need not be the syndrome of a small data error.

The operation needed is therefore the following.

Let

$$H:\mathbb F_2^n\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2^r$$

be one CSS syndrome map. Given

$$y=s+f,\qquad s\in\operatorname{im}H,$$

where only the measurement error $f$ is small, construct a valid syndrome $\widehat s$ such that

$$\widehat s+s=Hg$$

for some small data error $g$. The algorithm must produce $\widehat s$; it need not identify the unknown $f$ or the particular small lift $g$.

The achieved contract is

$$|f|\le\chi n
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\widehat s\in\operatorname{im}H,\qquad
\widehat s+s=Hg,\qquad
|g|\le K|f|,
\tag{1}$$

with fixed computable $\chi>0$ and $K<\infty$.

This is a promised nearby-valid-syndrome problem. It does not claim to solve unrestricted nearest-syndrome optimization.

2.1 Construction in the upper CSS sector

Write the represented complex as

$$C^0\xrightarrow{\delta^0}C^1\xrightarrow{\delta^1}C^2
\xrightarrow{\delta^2}C^3\xrightarrow{\delta^3}C^4
\xrightarrow{\delta^4}C^5\xrightarrow{\delta^5}C^6.$$

The data occupy $C^3$. Let the coefficient field be $\mathbb F_{2^r}$, with fixed $r$, and let $D$ be the fixed maximum directional degree. Write $z_j$ for the number of $j$-faces.

Choose fixed local parameters giving

$$m^j(\mathcal F),m^j(\mathcal K)\ge c z_j,
\qquad j=3,4,5,
\tag{2}$$

for a computable rational $c>0$, where $\mathcal K$ is the auxiliary kernel cosheaf. The relevant locally cominimal-distance theorem applies in every degree below six. Strengthening the fixed spectral margin obtains these three degrees simultaneously; nothing is weakened as the block size grows. The local filling operations used below are the accepted local-descent and anchored-array constructions. arxiv.org [https://arxiv.org/html/2609.20780v1?utm_source=chatgpt.com]

$$y=s+f\in C^4,\qquad s\in\operatorname{im}\delta^3.$$

$$b=\delta^4y=\delta^4f.$$

Because $\delta^4\delta^3=0$, the unknown valid component disappears. In face-block weight,

3. Upper-sector syndrome cleaner

Take

$$s=s_0+f\in C^4,\qquad s_0\in\operatorname{im}\delta^3.$$

Compute the metasyndrome

$$b=\delta^4s=\delta^4f.$$

In face-block weight,

$$|b|_b\le2D|f|_b.$$

If

$$2D|f|_b<cZ_5,$$

the local-descent algorithm of Lemma 6.4.1 constructs $f'\in C^4$ such that

$$\delta^4 f'=b,\qquad
|f'|_b\le \ell_4|b|_b.$$

Therefore $q=f+f'$ is a cocycle and

$$|q|_b\le(1+2D\ell_4)|f|_b.$$

If additionally

$$(1+2D\ell_4)|f|_b<cZ_4,$$

cosystolic distance implies

$$q\in\operatorname{im}\delta^3.$$

Consequently $s+f'$ is a valid syndrome.

A second application of local descent establishes a lift $g\in C^3$ with

$$\delta^3g=q,\qquad
|g|_b\le\ell_3(1+2D\ell_4)|f|_b.$$

Converting the data lift to binary weight gives

$$|g|_H\le K_+|f|_H,
\qquad
K_+=sD^3\ell_3(1+2D\ell_4).$$

Only $f'$ and an arbitrary linear preimage of $s+f'$ are computed during known-state preparation. The second small lift is an analysis certificate.

4. Lower-sector syndrome cleaner

Take

$$s=s_0+f\in(C^2)^*,\qquad s_0\in\operatorname{im}B_3.$$

Compute

$$b=B_2s=B_2f.$$

Each two-face has four one-dimensional facets, so

$$|b|_b\le4|f|_b.$$

Apply Proposition 7.3.3 with $k=1$. Under

$$4|f|_b<cZ_5/B,$$

its construction yields $f'\in(C^2)^*$ satisfying

$$B_2f'=b,\qquad
|f'|_b\le\frac{4T}{\eta_4}|f|_b.$$

Then $q=f+f'$ is a cycle. If

$$\left(1+\frac{4T}{\eta_4}\right)|f|_b<cZ_4/B,$$

Proposition 7.3.3 with $k=2$ gives

$$q=B_3g,\qquad
|g|_b\le
\frac{T}{\eta_3}
\left(1+\frac{4T}{\eta_4}\right)|f|_b.$$

Hence

$$|g|_H\le K_-|f|_H,
\qquad
K_-=sD^3\frac{T}{\eta_3}
\left(1+\frac{4T}{\eta_4}\right).$$

No hidden minimum-weight primitive

The small-cycle proof lifts through constant-size anchored-array maps. Its final cocycle lies in degree five or four of $\mathcal K$, below the corresponding locally cominimal distance. The required primitive is therefore obtained by the same finite local-descent search from Lemma 6.4.1. Local right inverses are computed by constant-dimensional Gaussian elimination.

This replaces the nonconstructive choice of a minimum-size primitive with an actual algorithm on the represented complex.

5. Explicit promise thresholds

Put

$$R_j=\frac{Z_j}{N}.$$

A conservative common syndrome-error threshold is

\frac12\min\left\{

\frac{cR_5}{4B},
